info.title: MailHQ API
info.description:
## Domain onboarding guide

Send and receive mail with your own domain. The domain can stay at its current registrar. An admin requests onboarding and verifies domain ownership; once DNS is configured with the records shown in the admin, you can use your own email addresses.

[Start domain onboarding](/settings#domain-connection) · [Admin](/settings) · [Webmail](/webmail)

### 01 · Request onboarding

Prepare a domain whose DNS you control. In **Settings → External domain onboarding**, an admin selects a Stalwart mail service subscription, enters the domain (for example `example.com`) and clicks **Generate verification record**.

Only admins can request, verify and view onboarding settings. Domains and mailboxes are currently managed centrally by admins; domain owners never need to hand over registrar accounts or DNS keys to this service.

Admin tip: once provisioned, the domain joins the existing mailbox management and redemption rules. Generic redemption codes or products without a domain restriction will include the new domain; before hosting an external domain, review and restrict the allowed domains.

### 02 · Add a TXT record to verify ownership

1. In the admin, open the domain's onboarding details and copy the name and value of the **Domain ownership** TXT record.
2. At the DNS provider the domain currently uses, add that TXT record. Whether the host field needs the full domain depends on your provider; avoid appending the domain suffix twice.
3. Wait for DNS to propagate, then click **Verify ownership and connect** in the admin. Once verified, the domain is provisioned on the mail server and added to the managed list.

Pending verification records are valid for 7 days; after that, click **Refresh verification record**, update the value in DNS and verify again. Ownership of an already provisioned domain does not expire because of this. You can keep the verification TXT for auditing; removing it does not disable a provisioned domain. No MX change is needed at this stage, so existing mailboxes keep receiving mail.

If the page shows **Confirming provisioning**, use **Check again** to read the result; if it shows **Needs manual review**, an admin should check the domain on the server first to avoid creating it twice.

### 03 · Prepare mailboxes, then migrate mail

Provisioning status and mail DNS checks are shown separately. Once ownership verification and server provisioning are done, you can create mailboxes on the domain, such as `you@example.com`, without switching mail routing first.

If the domain already has mailboxes, create the matching accounts and confirm passwords and forwarding rules before migrating any old mail you want to keep. Creating a mailbox does not copy historical mail from the old provider.

Move on only once the new mailboxes are ready. For a while after switching MX, some senders may still use the old records, so keep the old service and check mail on both sides.

### 04 · Configure mail DNS from the admin, switch MX last

In **Settings → Domains**, click the domain's **DNS settings / check**, or open its details from the onboarding request list. The admin shows the exact names, values, MX priorities and check results this domain needs. Use those records; the table below explains what each kind is for.

| Record | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MX | Delivers new mail to this service | Use the target and priority shown in the admin; switch it last, once mailboxes and migration are ready. |
| TXT · SPF | Authorizes servers to send for the domain | A domain can have only one SPF record. If one exists, merge the authorizations and keep other sending services still in use. |
| TXT · DKIM | Verifies mail signatures | Copy each selector and public key exactly as shown in the admin. Do not use signing records from other domains or servers. |
| TXT · DMARC | Declares the mail authentication policy | Optional and recommended; start with `p=none`. If a policy exists, review it first and do not overwrite existing quarantine or reject policies. |

Set mail-related records to **DNS only**; do not enable web proxying. Unless an admin says otherwise, there is no need to create `mail.your-domain` or get a certificate for it; mail clients use the server name shown in the admin.

Before switching MX, review the domain settings at the old provider. Some providers may still deliver mail sent within their own platform to their old mailboxes, so the old provider's delivery mode may also need adjusting.

### 05 · Check again and start using it

After saving DNS, click **Check again** in the domain details. The page shows the records currently found and why any are missing, conflicting or failed to resolve. DNS caches take time to update; if records don't match yet, confirm the names and values, then wait for the old records' caches to expire.

| Item | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Incoming mail | IMAP · 993 · SSL/TLS |
| Outgoing mail | SMTP · 465 · SSL/TLS |
| Server | The server name shown on the admin page |
| Sign-in | Full email address + mailbox password |

Use [Webmail](/webmail) or your own mail client. Whether webmail is available depends on the domain being provisioned and the settings an admin has enabled.

Test receiving and sending separately from an independent external mailbox, and check the spam folder. Passing DNS checks and SPF / DKIM / DMARC does not guarantee delivery to the inbox at Gmail or other services.

The live settings on the admin page are authoritative for each domain's records. [Manage domain onboarding](/settings#domain-connection).

## API access

### Creating keys and authenticating

First generate an API key in [Settings → API keys](/settings/api-keys), choosing the permissions and expiry you need (it can be set to never expire), then enter the full key under Authorize.

All `/api/v1` endpoints accept only `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`. A browser sign-in cookie cannot replace a Bearer key, and each operation also requires the matching scope. Granting only a write scope does not grant read access. After a key is revoked, further requests with it are rejected.

### Scope

This API manages the Stalwart mail service connected to MailHQ.

It currently covers the server list, domain verification and provisioning, importing existing domains, enabling/disabling domains, mailboxes, passwords, status, storage quota, daily sending limits, notes, regular aliases, distribution lists, forwarding, a per-domain catch-all, alias domains and domain connection details, with batch operations. It does not offer reading/searching/deleting mail content, sending mail, autoresponders, spam policies or reseller management.

Below, each operation's scope, parameters, responses and examples are listed by group. The API base URL is `/api/v1` on this site.

### Regular aliases and domain management

Regular aliases use the `aliases:read` / `aliases:write` scopes. The target must be an existing managed user mailbox on the same domain; aliases can be created, renamed, enabled/disabled, re-described and deleted, but the target mailbox cannot be changed. Special or read-only aliases must be managed in Stalwart. Aliases are neither external forwarding nor catch-all.

`GET /domains/{id}/catch-all` reads and `PUT /domains/{id}/catch-all` sets the mailbox that receives mail for addresses of the domain nobody holds: `{ "destination": "postmaster@example.com" }` (an existing managed mailbox of the same domain), or `{ "destination": null }` to reject such mail, the default. A catch-all accepts every guessed or mistyped address, so it attracts spam.

`PUT /domains/{id}/status` accepts `{ "enabled": true }` or `false` and enables or disables the domain on Stalwart. `DELETE /domains/{id}` still only removes the local record and cannot delete the remote domain. Writes to domains and aliases require the admin role and the matching write scope.

### Alias domains

An alias domain is an additional domain name whose addresses deliver to the mailboxes of a primary domain: mail for `user@alias.example` goes to the mailbox of `user@primary.example`, and the primary domain's aliases, lists and catch-all apply too. `POST /domains/{id}/domain-aliases` with `{ "domain": "alias.example" }` records the request and returns the ownership TXT record; after publishing it, `POST /domains/{id}/domain-aliases/{aliasId}/verify` adds the name on the mail server, and `GET` on the alias lists the MX record it needs to receive mail. An alias domain is for receiving: mail sent from its addresses is signed with the primary domain's DKIM key. Onboard a domain of its own when it has to send under its own name.

### Distribution lists

Distribution lists use the `lists:read` / `lists:write` scopes. A list is an address of a domain that delivers a copy of every message to all of its members; it has no mailbox, cannot sign in and does not count towards the workspace's mailbox limit. `GET /lists?domainId=…` lists a domain's lists with their members, `POST /lists` creates one, and `PATCH /lists/{listId}` renames it, changes its description and adds or removes members. Members that are not mailboxes managed by the workspace are refused unless the request sets `allowExternal: true`: the mail server then forwards everything sent to the list, spam included, to those outside addresses. The list's address must be free among mailboxes (pending and deleted ones included), aliases, forwarding addresses and other lists.

### Legal holds

Legal holds use the `holds:read` / `holds:write` scopes (admin keys only). `POST /holds` places a hold on one mailbox (`mailboxId`) or on every mailbox of a domain (`domain`) with a `name`, a `reason` and an optional `endsAt`; `POST /holds/{id}/release` releases it with a `reason`. While a hold is active the mailbox cannot be deleted permanently or purged from the recycle bin (`409 legal_hold`); deleting it into the recycle bin still works. A hold preserves the mailbox, not individual messages: the mailbox's user can still delete their own mail, and this is not a certified archive.

### Reports

`GET /reports/inactive-mailboxes`, `GET /reports/storage` and `GET /reports/top-senders` are read-only reports under `mailboxes:read`: mailboxes with no WebMail sign-in and no mail for 30, 60 or 90 days, mailbox usage per domain from daily samples, and today's top senders by daily sending-limit usage. They are computed from records MailHQ keeps, not from the mail server's own counters: sign-ins and sends of mail apps over IMAP / SMTP are not seen.

### Batch requests and verifying results

`POST /batch` accepts `{ "operations": [...] }` with 1–25 operations and a body of at most 16 KiB, and requires an `Idempotency-Key` of 8–128 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores. Each operation has a unique `id`, an `operation` and an `input`. The whole request's format, base fields and required scopes are validated before the first write, then operations run in order; resource existence, domain ownership and remote state are checked as each one runs.

Returns 200 when everything succeeds and 207 when any operation failed, is uncertain or was not executed. Each `outcome` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `uncertain` or `skipped`. Execution continues after ordinary failures and stops when a result is unclear; completed operations are not rolled back or retried automatically, and responses never include passwords.

The same API key, idempotency key and normalized operations replay the saved result; different content returns 409. After a timeout, first query `GET /batch/{requestId}` with the original key: it returns only the `running` / `completed` / `uncertain` state and timestamps, not the operations or results. `running` and `uncertain` never expire or re-run automatically. Even when it reports `completed`, still check every outcome in the original batch result; it does not mean every operation succeeded.

### Interactive requests and documentation security

All examples use fictional data. The documentation never reads instance configuration, connected domains, mailbox passwords or API keys.

Interactive requests go directly from your browser to this site, without a public request proxy. Keys are not kept after a page refresh; do not enter API keys on shared devices, and never put keys in URLs, code repositories or logs.

x-error-codes.meaning: The request body is over 16 KiB (8 MiB for POST /emails and /emails/batch).
x-error-codes.action: Send less per request; use several requests or a batch.

x-error-codes.meaning: The operation was retired after its announced sunset date.
x-error-codes.action: Use the replacement in `details.replacement`; see the API changelog.

x-error-codes.meaning: The request sent a field, query parameter or enum value retired after its sunset date.
x-error-codes.action: Drop it or use `details.replacement`; `details.field` names it.

x-error-codes.meaning: The key lacks a scope the operation needs, or its owner's current role no longer allows it.
x-error-codes.action: Create a key with the scope listed for the operation in the reference, owned by an account whose role allows it.

x-error-codes.meaning: An MCP tool was called with arguments that are not a JSON object of the tool's own fields.
x-error-codes.action: Pass exactly the fields in the tool's input schema.

x-error-codes.meaning: An ID in the path or body is not in the format of a record ID.
x-error-codes.action: Use the IDs the API returns.

x-error-codes.meaning: The body is not valid JSON, or not a JSON object.
x-error-codes.action: Send a JSON object.

x-error-codes.meaning: A query parameter is unknown, malformed or out of range.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the parameter `details` names; the reference lists each operation's parameters and their ranges.

x-error-codes.meaning: The path exists but not with this HTTP method.
x-error-codes.action: Use one of the methods in the `Allow` header.

x-error-codes.meaning: The record in the path does not exist in this workspace (or is in the recycle bin, for mailboxes).
x-error-codes.action: Check the ID: paths take the record IDs the API returns, not addresses or domain names.

x-error-codes.meaning: The key's (or the address's) rate limit is used up for this window; nothing was done.
x-error-codes.action: Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again. Use batches for bulk changes.

x-error-codes.meaning: No Bearer key was sent, or the key is unknown, expired, revoked or no longer valid for its owner.
x-error-codes.action: Send a working key in `Authorization: Bearer`. Repeated invalid keys get the sending address rate-limited.

x-error-codes.meaning: The body has a field the operation does not take.
x-error-codes.action: Remove it; `details` names it.

x-error-codes.meaning: A request body was sent without `Content-Type: application/json`.
x-error-codes.action: Send JSON with that content type.

x-error-codes.meaning: The alias domain changed while the request ran.
x-error-codes.action: Read it again, then decide whether to repeat the request.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain already has the most alias domains allowed.
x-error-codes.action: Remove one before adding another.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain, alias domain or address already exists (here, or claimed by another workspace).
x-error-codes.action: Use the existing record, or choose another name.

x-error-codes.meaning: The DNS lookup for the ownership check failed; nothing was changed.
x-error-codes.action: Try again later.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain's server binding is ambiguous or changed while the request ran.
x-error-codes.action: Have an admin review the domain's binding, then try again.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain's binding changed while the request ran.
x-error-codes.action: Read the domain again, then decide whether to repeat the request.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain still has alias domains.
x-error-codes.action: Remove its alias domains first.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain still has local mailboxes, so its record cannot be removed.
x-error-codes.action: Delete or move its mailboxes first.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain to import is not on the chosen server.
x-error-codes.action: Create it on that server first, or onboard it with `/domain-onboardings`.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain's onboarding has not finished, or its state does not allow this step.
x-error-codes.action: Read the onboarding's state and DNS status; never submit the remote provisioning twice.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain cannot be imported without a verified ownership onboarding in this workspace.
x-error-codes.action: Onboard it with `/domain-onboardings` instead.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain is not bound to a valid mail server, so nothing on it can be changed remotely.
x-error-codes.action: Bind the domain to a server in the admin console.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain name is missing or not a valid name.
x-error-codes.action: Send a lowercase domain name such as example.com.

x-error-codes.meaning: The status change does not say whether to enable or disable the domain.
x-error-codes.action: Send `{ "enabled": true }` or `{ "enabled": false }`.

x-error-codes.meaning: The ownership TXT record was not found with the expected value.
x-error-codes.action: Publish the record the connection details show, wait for DNS, then verify again.

x-error-codes.meaning: Deleting a domain on the mail server is not offered.
x-error-codes.action: Disable the domain, then remove only the local record; the server keeps the domain and its data.

x-error-codes.meaning: The mail server in `subscriptionId` does not exist or is not available to this workspace.
x-error-codes.action: Use an ID from `GET /servers`.

x-error-codes.meaning: Several mail servers are configured and the request does not say which one to use.
x-error-codes.action: Send `subscriptionId` (one of `GET /servers`).

x-error-codes.meaning: The alias domain's ownership value expired before it was verified.
x-error-codes.action: Remove the alias domain, add it again and publish the new value.

x-error-codes.meaning: The daily sending limit is not an integer in range.
x-error-codes.action: Send an integer from 0 to 1000000.

x-error-codes.meaning: The mailbox fields failed validation.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the fields listed in `details.fields`.

x-error-codes.meaning: The bulk sending-limit request does not name 1–100 distinct mailbox IDs.
x-error-codes.action: Send between 1 and 100 distinct mailbox record IDs.

x-error-codes.meaning: The note (of a mailbox or a suppression) is too long or not text.
x-error-codes.action: Send at most the documented number of characters.

x-error-codes.meaning: The password is not 8–128 characters without whitespace.
x-error-codes.action: Send a password that meets the rule.

x-error-codes.meaning: The quota is not a whole number of MB in range.
x-error-codes.action: Send an integer from 0 (no limit) to the documented maximum.

x-error-codes.meaning: The status is not one of `active`, `disabled` or `pending`.
x-error-codes.action: Send one of those values.

x-error-codes.meaning: The username (the part before @) is not valid.
x-error-codes.action: Use 1–64 lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

x-error-codes.meaning: The mailbox write was sent to the server but its result is not confirmed; a pending record was kept.
x-error-codes.action: Look the mailbox up with `details.mailboxId` and verify it; do not create it again.

x-error-codes.meaning: A sending limit cannot be set for this mailbox (not created on the server yet, or not supported).
x-error-codes.action: Create the mailbox first, or leave the limit to the server's default.

x-error-codes.meaning: The sending-limit write may or may not have been applied.
x-error-codes.action: Read the limit back (GET); repeat only the same target value, never a different one, if it is not set.

x-error-codes.meaning: The address is already used by a mailbox, service mailbox, alias, list, forwarder or a mailbox in the recycle bin.
x-error-codes.action: Choose another address.

x-error-codes.meaning: The list has members outside the workspace's domains, which this workspace does not allow.
x-error-codes.action: Remove the outside addresses, or ask an admin to allow external members.

x-error-codes.meaning: The rule forwards to itself or would close a loop with existing forwarding.
x-error-codes.action: Choose a different destination.

x-error-codes.meaning: The alias fields are invalid.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the username, target or description.

x-error-codes.meaning: The alias target is not an existing managed mailbox of the same domain.
x-error-codes.action: Point the alias at a mailbox of its own domain.

x-error-codes.meaning: The catch-all setting is invalid.
x-error-codes.action: Send a mailbox address of the domain, or null to reject mail to unknown addresses.

x-error-codes.meaning: The catch-all destination is not an existing managed mailbox of this domain.
x-error-codes.action: Use one of the domain's own mailboxes.

x-error-codes.meaning: The forwarding rule's source or destination is invalid.
x-error-codes.action: Send one source address of the domain and one destination address.

x-error-codes.meaning: The distribution list fields are invalid.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the username, description or members.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain already has the most distribution lists allowed.
x-error-codes.action: Delete a list before creating another.

x-error-codes.meaning: This alias is a special one managed on the mail server (or a user's masked address) and cannot be changed here.
x-error-codes.action: Leave it as it is.

x-error-codes.meaning: This rule is not managed here (a list, alias, catch-all or custom Sieve rule).
x-error-codes.action: Change it where it is managed.

x-error-codes.meaning: This list is managed on the mail server and cannot be changed here.
x-error-codes.action: Leave it as it is.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain's mail server does not support this kind of address management.
x-error-codes.action: Use a Stalwart 1.0 or later server for the domain.

x-error-codes.meaning: An item of a batch that was not run because an earlier item's outcome is unconfirmed (item `error.code`).
x-error-codes.action: Verify the earlier item, then send this one again in a new batch.

x-error-codes.meaning: This idempotency key was already used, with this key, for a different batch (or follow-up task, or messages sent through /emails).
x-error-codes.action: Use a new idempotency key for different content.

x-error-codes.meaning: A batch with this idempotency key is still running.
x-error-codes.action: Read its state with `GET /batch/{requestId}`; do not resend under another key.

x-error-codes.meaning: A batch with this idempotency key stopped with an unconfirmed write.
x-error-codes.action: Verify the affected records, then send only what is confirmed missing, in a new batch with a new key.

x-error-codes.meaning: The batch body is invalid: not 1–25 operations, duplicate item IDs, an unknown operation or bad input; for `POST /emails/batch`, `emails` is not a list of 1 to 50 messages.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the batch; nothing in it was run or sent.

x-error-codes.meaning: The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing or not 8–128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.
x-error-codes.action: Send a valid key, unique per batch.

x-error-codes.meaning: The batch reached its request budget on the mail server and the remaining operations were stopped.
x-error-codes.action: Check the results, then send the rest in smaller batches.

x-error-codes.meaning: The delivery is still waiting for its own retry.
x-error-codes.action: Only a delivered or dead-lettered delivery can be sent again; wait for it to settle.

x-error-codes.meaning: The description is longer than 200 characters.
x-error-codes.action: Shorten it.

x-error-codes.meaning: `enabled` is not a boolean.
x-error-codes.action: Send true or false.

x-error-codes.meaning: The events list names an unknown event type.
x-error-codes.action: Use the event types in the reference, or `["*"]`.

x-error-codes.meaning: A webhook update changes nothing.
x-error-codes.action: Send at least one of `url`, `description`, `events` and `enabled`.

x-error-codes.meaning: `format` is not standard, feishu or dingtalk, `botSecret` came without a bot format or is not one, or a PATCH tried to change either (they are set when the webhook is made).
x-error-codes.action: Send one of the formats, and a bot's signing secret only with a bot format; to change the format, make a new webhook.

x-error-codes.meaning: The address is not https on the default port with a public host name, or, for a bot format, not that bot platform's webhook address.
x-error-codes.action: Use a public https address without credentials, IP literal or internal name.

x-error-codes.meaning: The workspace already has the most webhooks allowed (10).
x-error-codes.action: Delete one before creating another.

x-error-codes.meaning: The legal hold was already released or has ended.
x-error-codes.action: Nothing to release; place a new hold if needed.

x-error-codes.meaning: The suppression list address is not a valid email address.
x-error-codes.action: Send one valid address.

x-error-codes.meaning: The hold's end date is not a future ISO 8601 time.
x-error-codes.action: Send a future date, or none.

x-error-codes.meaning: The required reason is missing or too long.
x-error-codes.action: Send a reason.

x-error-codes.meaning: A trace search names none of sender, recipient, Message-ID or queue ID.
x-error-codes.action: Give at least one of them.

x-error-codes.meaning: No mail server whose logs can be read is configured.
x-error-codes.action: Ask an admin to connect a mail server.

x-error-codes.meaning: This email awaiting approval was already approved or rejected.
x-error-codes.action: Read the task's approvals again.

x-error-codes.meaning: An admin switched automatic sending off, so every email of a task needs approval.
x-error-codes.action: Create the task with approval required, or ask an admin.

x-error-codes.meaning: The follow-up task's fields are invalid.
x-error-codes.action: Fix what the message describes.

x-error-codes.meaning: The task is not in a state that allows this (only a running task can be paused, a paused one resumed).
x-error-codes.action: Read the task's state first.

x-error-codes.meaning: The task's mailbox cannot be used (disabled, no stored password, or its domain has no mail server).
x-error-codes.action: Fix the mailbox, or use another one.

x-error-codes.meaning: The task has already ended.
x-error-codes.action: Create a new task if more follow-up is needed.

x-error-codes.meaning: The attachments are over 5 MiB in all, decoded.
x-error-codes.action: Send smaller files, or a link to them.

x-error-codes.meaning: The workspace's plan bills sending through the API, and the workspace has no subscription that may send (none, canceled, unpaid).
x-error-codes.action: An admin subscribes, or fixes the payment, under Settings → Developers → Billing. `details.status` is the subscription's Stripe status.

x-error-codes.meaning: The domain does not send through the API, so it has no sending account to make SMTP relay credentials for.
x-error-codes.action: Turn sending on for the domain (`PUT /domains/{id}/sending`) first.

x-error-codes.meaning: Sending through the API is not turned on for this workspace: a platform admin has not approved it.
x-error-codes.action: Ask the platform's operator to approve it (with a daily limit). Test keys can send to the sandbox meanwhile.

x-error-codes.meaning: Live sending is paused for the workspace: in the last 7 days (or since it was last resumed) too many recipients bounced or complained. `details.reason` says which, `details.pausedAt` since when.
x-error-codes.action: Find out why (a stale list, a missing unsubscribe, a stolen key) and fix it, then ask the platform's operator to resume sending. Test keys still send to the sandbox.

x-error-codes.meaning: The workspace's daily allowance of messages is used up (a batch counts all of its messages).
x-error-codes.action: Send again after `details.resetAt` (midnight UTC), or ask for a higher limit. Nothing of the request was sent.

x-error-codes.meaning: The From address is not on a domain of this workspace that sends through the API.
x-error-codes.action: Turn sending on for the domain (`PUT /domains/{id}/sending`), or send from a domain that has it. `details.index` names the message in a batch.

x-error-codes.meaning: An agent mailbox's `name` is not a single line of at most 200 characters without quotes or angle brackets.
x-error-codes.action: Fix it.

x-error-codes.meaning: An attachment is malformed: no filename, content that is not base64, a bad content type, or more than 10 attachments.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the attachments.

x-error-codes.meaning: The message has neither `text` nor `html`, or one of them is too long.
x-error-codes.action: Send `text`, `html` or both, within the documented sizes.

x-error-codes.meaning: `from` is not an address or `Name <address>`.
x-error-codes.action: Fix it.

x-error-codes.meaning: `headers` holds a header that is not allowed (only X- headers, List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post), repeats one, or has a multi-line value.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the headers.

x-error-codes.meaning: A mail app needs a name, 1 to 5 redirect URIs (https on a public host, or http on the loopback) and scopes from mail.read, mail.send and mail.modify.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the app.

x-error-codes.meaning: A change to an agent mailbox's message needs `read` and/or `flagged`, each true or false, and nothing else.
x-error-codes.action: Send `{ "read": true }`, `{ "flagged": false }` or both.

x-error-codes.meaning: `to`, `cc`, `bcc` or `replyTo` holds something that is not an address, or the message has no recipient or more than 50.
x-error-codes.action: Fix the lists; send to more people in several messages or a batch.

x-error-codes.meaning: An SMTP relay credential needs a name: one line of at most 100 characters.
x-error-codes.action: Name what the credential is for (the application that will use it).

x-error-codes.meaning: `subject` is missing, empty, over 500 characters or not a single line.
x-error-codes.action: Fix it.

x-error-codes.meaning: `tags` is not an object of up to 10 names with string values.

tags.name: Domain onboarding
tags.description: Provision a domain after verifying ownership, or look up / cancel pending requests.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Import existing Stalwart domains and manage local records.

tags.name: Mailboxes
tags.description: Manage mailboxes; passwords and redemption-code links are never returned.

tags.name: Forwarders
tags.description: Forwarding rules between single regular email addresses.

tags.name: Aliases
tags.description: Regular aliases delivering to managed mailboxes on the same domain.

tags.name: Lists
tags.description: Distribution lists: an address of a domain that delivers to all of its members.

tags.name: Legal holds
tags.description: Legal holds: a held mailbox cannot be deleted permanently or purged. A hold preserves the mailbox, not individual messages.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Usage reports: inactive mailboxes, storage per domain, top senders. Computed from this app's own records.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description: Manage domains, mailboxes and aliases in ordered batches with persisted idempotent results.

tags.name: Agent tasks
tags.description: An agent follows up email as a given mailbox: it starts from a prompt, sends fully autonomously by default, and continues when replies arrive.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Signed event webhooks: mailbox, domain, order, bulk job and security events POSTed to your https address, with retries and a delivery log.

tags.name: Trace
tags.description: Message trace: the delivery timeline of messages sent or received by the workspace's domains, read from the mail server's logs and queue. Every call is recorded in the activity log.

tags.name: Emails
tags.description: Send mail from the workspace's domains through their own mail server, and follow each message's delivery. Off until a platform admin approves the workspace; test keys send to the sandbox.

tags.name: Inbound
tags.description: Inbound routing: mail that chosen mailboxes receive is POSTed to webhooks as message.received, and can be read through the API.

tags.name: Agent mailboxes
tags.description: A mailbox an AI agent reads and sends from, made in one call, and a key restricted to just that mailbox for the agent itself.

tags.name: Mail apps
tags.description: Third-party apps a workspace registers so its mailbox users can authorize them, with OAuth on WebMail, to read their mail or send as them through WebMail's Mail API.

tags.name: Suppressions
tags.description: The workspace's suppression list: recipients that hard-bounced repeatedly or were added by hand. Advisory: nothing is refused at submission; check an address before sending to it.

get.description:
Requires `trace:read` scope.

What happened to a message: when it was accepted and queued, every delivery attempt with the remote host and its SMTP answer, and whether it ended delivered, deferred (with the next retry) or bounced. At least one of `sender`, `recipient`, `messageId` and `queueId` is required (400 `missing_criteria`); all given criteria must match.

The data comes from the mail server's file logs (Stalwart's own per-message history is Enterprise-only), so only messages still in the logs are found, and steps such as TLS are present only when the server logs them; `tls` and `dkimSigned` are `null` when the log does not say. `queued` lists matching messages still waiting in the outbound queue, read from the queue itself. Each call reads a bounded part of the logs and returns at most 10 messages; while `cursor` is not null, call again with it for older ones. `servers[].exhausted` says nothing more of the workspace's messages was found on that server.

**Off until the platform operator turns it on**: while the platform setting "Workspace admins can use message trace" is off (the default), only a platform admin's key of the default workspace may call this; every other key gets `403 forbidden`, also with the `trace:read` scope.

A key sees only messages whose envelope sender or a recipient is in one of its workspace's domains, and of a message from outside only the recipients in those domains. Nothing else in the answer comes from other workspaces' mail either: `searchedBack`, `servers[].oldest`, `servers[].exhausted` and `cursor` are worked out from the key's own messages, so a search that only other workspaces' mail matches answers exactly like one that nothing matches. To page reliably through mail from a sender who also writes to other workspaces, add one of the workspace's own addresses or domains as `recipient`. **Every call is recorded in the activity log** with the key's id and the search terms, because a trace reveals who wrote to whom. 409 `trace_unavailable`: none of the workspace's domains is bound to a mail server whose management API is configured.
